items.q: The network shows the activities in a project (durations in days). What is the length of the critical path?
items.why: Node 2: earliest start = 3. Node 3: the largest of A+B = 9, A+C = 10 and E = 11, so 11. Node 4: 11 + 2 = 13. The critical path is E–D, taking 13 days.

items.q: A business has sales of £92m in a market worth £746m. What is its market share?
items.why: Market share = business sales ÷ total market sales × 100 = 92 ÷ 746 × 100 = 12.3%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has 50 employees who are each expected to work 230 days a year. 1,120 working days were lost to absence. What is the absenteeism rate?
items.why: Absenteeism = days lost ÷ total possible working days × 100 = 1,120 ÷ (50 × 230) × 100 = 1,120 ÷ 11,500 × 100 = 9.74%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company achieved a ROCE of 15% with capital employed of £290m. What was its operating profit?
items.why: ROCE = operating profit ÷ capital employed × 100, so operating profit = ROCE × capital employed = 15% × £290m = £43.5m.
items.label: New question

items.q: Market grew 2% from £670 million in 2015. New sales revenue?
items.why: 670m x 1.02 = 683.4m. Or: 670 + (670 x 0.02) = 670 + 13.4 = £683.4 million. Option A is just the growth amount. Option B adds 2 not 2%.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Magpie plc (all figures £m): sales revenue 80, cost of sales 50, bank overdraft 7, inventory 8, payables 12, receivables 17. These are all its current assets and current liabilities, and inventory is the same as the average for the year. Calculate its inventory turnover.
items.why: Inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = £50m ÷ £8m = 6.25 times. Use cost of sales, not revenue (which would give 10).
items.label: Paper 1 June 2022 Q16

items.q: A project costs £200,000 and lasts 5 years. Net cash flows are Year 1: £210,000; Year 2: £190,000; Year 3: £190,000; Year 4: £190,000; Year 5: £220,000. What is the average rate of return (ARR)?
items.why: Total net cash flow = £1,000,000. Total profit = £1,000,000 – £200,000 = £800,000. Average annual profit = £800,000 ÷ 5 = £160,000. ARR = £160,000 ÷ £200,000 × 100 = 80%. Taking off the cost of the investment is the step most often missed.
items.label: New question

items.q: A product has a price elasticity of demand of -0.5. The price falls by 10%. What happens to quantity demanded and sales revenue?
items.why: % change in quantity = PED × % change in price = -0.5 × -10% = +5%. Demand is inelastic, so revenue moves the same way as price: it falls.
